diagnosis.summary: Cart-service has been classified as a DATABASE_THROTTLING incident. In this one-minute window all DynamoDB throttle counts are zero, p95 end-to-end latency is 8.33 ms against a baseline of 8.87 ms, and 5xx error rate is zero. Request rate has risen from 2.05 to 3.57 rps, a 74% increase.
diagnosis.root_cause: DynamoDB throttling on the cart-service table is the most likely root cause, though in this window throttled_requests, read_throttle_events, and write_throttle_events all remain at zero with no latency elevation or 5xx errors present.
evidence: All three DynamoDB throttle counters — throttled_requests, read_throttle_events, and write_throttle_events — are at 0, unchanged from their baseline of 0.
db_latency_ms_p95 is 5.63 ms, slightly below its baseline of 6.58 ms, showing no tail-latency elevation in DynamoDB calls.
error_rate_5xx is 0, identical to its baseline of 0, with no failed requests in this window.
p95_latency_ms is 8.33 ms against a baseline of 8.87 ms, within normal range and not elevated.
request_rate rose from 2.05 rps to 3.57 rps, a 74% increase above baseline.
db_consumed_read_capacity is 0 in both baseline and current, indicating no read capacity was consumed in this window.
recommended_actions: Monitor read_throttle_events and throttled_requests on the cart-service table closely over the next several minutes given the 74% rise in request_rate, as throttling may emerge if the elevated rate persists.
Check db_consumed_read_capacity in the next window to confirm whether the increased request rate is driving higher DynamoDB read consumption.
Recheck db_latency_ms_p95 and p95_latency_ms for any tail-latency growth that would indicate SDK retries beginning to accumulate inside DynamoDB calls.
If throttle counts rise, review the cart-service DynamoDB table capacity mode and consider whether the table's current configuration can sustain the observed request rate.
Watch error_rate_5xx for any increase, which would indicate requests exhausting all retry attempts against DynamoDB.
